I think the doctor called it "Borderline Peronsalit"? or something like that, ahahaha, you know it's crazy out there and I'm crazy about credit cars, which is why I want to get into that equity, so I can do all kinds of borderline things. nba_directive.reason_text: This client is close to ready but has a stated blocker (credit, income, or debt) — the highest-converting conditional-future profile. With a 2.75% VA loan and a $735/mo payment, a cash-out refi would be destructive; the winning move is a concrete blocker-removal plan paired with a HELOC/second-lien framing that protects their rate.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Open by protecting their 2.75% VA rate — make clear you will NOT touch it
  - Acknowledge their $735/mo payment is exceptional and irreplaceable
  - State explicitly: 'Any plan I build keeps that first mortgage exactly where it is'

- Name the blocker directly and hand them a concrete removal roadmap
  - Ask them to confirm the specific blocker (credit score gap, DTI, income docs) so you can tailor the path
  - If credit: identify the exact score needed for HELOC approval, pull a soft-credit snapshot today, and schedule a hard re-pull date once the gap is closed
  - If debt/DTI: show how consolidating high-rate balances via a HELOC can itself improve DTI — frame it as the blocker solving itself
  - Set a specific milestone date: 'Let's talk again on [date] — here's what you need to do between now and then'

- Reframe the HELOC rate against their actual debt costs
  - Credit cards are running 25–30% APR; a HELOC on $158,552 in equity will be a fraction of that
  - Calculate the monthly interest savings on their actual card/debt balances (ask them for the balances if not yet shared) — do not estimate a number you don't have
  - Present the HELOC as a debt-consolidation tool, not a rate play

- Anchor to their specific financial pain
  - Ask: 'What is the debt or expense that's putting the most pressure on you right now?'
  - Tie every number back to that answer — this is what converts

- Lock in the next concrete step before ending the text thread
  - Offer a 10-minute call to run the real numbers together
  - If they're not ready to call, send a one-item homework ask (e.g., 'Text me your highest-rate card balance and I'll show you the savings math tonight')
